network_thesis.headline: Türkiye's mobility super-app meets the world's busiest commuter waterway.
network_thesis.body: Türkiye's geography is water-first: Istanbul is a city split by a strait, İzmir is a city wrapped around a bay, and the Aegean-Mediterranean coast is one of the world's great leisure shorelines. Marti is Türkiye's home-grown mobility super-app — 4.3 million ride-hailing riders, half a million registered drivers, and the national e-scooter/e-bike/e-moped fleet. What Marti doesn't serve yet is the water its riders cross every day. A Navier foiling tier makes the Bosphorus, İzmir bay and the Aegean coast bookable in the app Türkiye already rides.

network_thesis.how_to_read: Each card is a real, ready market. Istanbul is the anchor — the world's busiest commuter waterway with a slow diesel incumbent. İzmir, Bodrum and Antalya extend the same fleet down the coast.
network_thesis.coverage_note: The same Navier fleet that anchors the four proposed markets extends across Marti's full operating footprint — Kocaeli's İzmit Bay and Mersin's Mediterranean shore are natural next water surfaces as corridors are mapped.

partner_context.their_ambition: You are Marti — Türkiye's mobility super-app and its only NYSE-listed tech champion. You built the national micromobility fleet (38,000+ electric two-wheelers across Istanbul, Ankara, İzmir, Antalya, Kocaeli, Muğla and Mersin), then stacked ride-hailing on top: 4.3 million riders and 532,000 registered drivers, growing ~96% a year.
partner_context.their_pressure: Ride-hailing in Türkiye is contested — commercially and politically. Your moat is being first, local and multimodal. The next defensible surface is the one no app has ever served: the water. Istanbul's cross-strait commute runs on slow diesel ferries; İzmir's bay hop is a timetable, not a tap; the Aegean leisure coast books boats over WhatsApp.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier turns Türkiye's water into a Marti tier: a software-defined foiling fleet, booked in the Marti app, premium-priced, on the Bosphorus, İzmir bay and the Bodrum-Antalya leisure coast — the same network model already ramping in the Maldives, on the busiest commuter waterway on earth.

hero.title: Marti × Navier — Türkiye's water, in the app
hero.subtitle: Istanbul is a city split by a strait. Marti is its super-app. The water between is the surface no one owns yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Marti-booked foiling water tier across Türkiye's busiest water surfaces — the Bosphorus and the Princes' Islands, İzmir bay, and the Bodrum and Antalya leisure coasts. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook now proven in the Maldives; Marti brings 4.3 million riders, the app, the wallet, and scooters at every pier. Together we turn the world's busiest commuter waterway into a fast, silent, all-electric tier of Türkiye's own super-app.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, dramatically more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives, and Türkiye's water is wide open — Şehir Hatları's diesel vapur average walking-pace crossings, İzmir's bay ferries run on timetables, and the Aegean coast has no premium on-demand tier at all.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — Istanbul's fifty-plus historic piers, İzmir's İzdeniz terminals, and the marinas of Bodrum and Antalya. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; no new terminals, no new charging network.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces converge on Marti's home turf: the technology crossed from prototype to platform; a ~100-vessel network is ramping in the Maldives; and Istanbul is electrifying its water — the municipality's own battery-electric vapur program proves the direction while leaving the premium, on-demand tier unclaimed.

multimodal_fit: Marti already runs the hardest parts: real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing, payments, a national two-wheeler fleet and a ride-hailing driver network. A foiling water tier slots straight in — same app, same wallet, captain-partners alongside TAG drivers, and a Marti scooter or moped staged at the pier so the Bosphorus crossing is door-to-door.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready — the same asset-tech instincts Marti built its fleet on (it acquired Boston AI firm Zoba for fleet optimization). A ~100-vessel at-scale network already proving the model in the Maldives, directly relevant to Türkiye's strait-bay-coast geography. And uniquely local: Türkiye's own super-app, not a foreign platform, claiming Türkiye's water.

proof_points.claim: The Bosphorus is one of the world's busiest commuter waterways.
proof_points.evidence: Şehir Hatları alone carries ~40M ferry passengers a year across more than fifty piers; the core cross-strait legs (Eminönü–Üsküdar, Karaköy–Kadıköy) are among the highest-frequency water corridors anywhere.
proof_points.source: Şehir Hatları ridership · Navier market coverage 2026

proof_points.claim: The legs are short by water.
proof_points.evidence: Eminönü–Üsküdar ~0.9nm, Karaköy–Kadıköy ~2.4nm, İzmir Konak–Karşıyaka ~2.5nm, Bostancı–Büyükada ~4.5nm — all deep inside Pioneer II range.

proof_points.claim: İzmir's bay is a second metro-scale water market.
proof_points.evidence: İzdeniz's Konak–Karşıyaka corridor carries ~14.6M passengers a year across a 2.5nm bay hop.

proof_points.claim: The Aegean-Med leisure coast is a committed expansion market.
proof_points.evidence: Bodrum's peninsula runs (Turgutreis, Gümüşlük, Yalıkavak, Datça) and Antalya's Kemer/Side corridors are mapped; Çeşme–Chios adds a ~7nm cross-border leg to Greece.

objections.concern: The Bosphorus is a busy, regulated shipping strait.
objections.response: We operate within the established ferry corridors and traffic rules; foiling craft are agile and low-wake, fitting the existing cross-strait pattern rather than the shipping lanes.

objections.concern: Public ferries already cross the Bosphorus cheaply.
objections.response: We add a premium, faster, on-demand tier in the Marti app for time-sensitive riders, complementing the mass vapur exactly as TAG complements the bus.

objections.concern: Ride-hailing in Türkiye faces regulatory headwinds.
objections.response: Water is a different regulatory surface: established ferry corridors, marine licensing, and a municipal electrification agenda that a zero-emission foiling tier advances rather than challenges.

objections.concern: Why Marti and not a global platform?
objections.response: Türkiye's water should be claimed by Türkiye's super-app — Marti has the local fleet, the local drivers, the local brand and the pier-side scooters no foreign app can stage.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, captain training, the maintenance & certification path, and a uniform integration spec.
the_ask.partner_brings: Riders, the app and wallet, pier-side scooter staging, and Istanbul as the launch market to prove the cross-strait tier.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a Phase-1 pilot (~4 vessels) on the core Bosphorus corridors (Eminönü–Üsküdar, Karaköy–Kadıköy), building out İzmir, the Princes' Islands and the Aegean coast as the network matures.

end_state.headline: The water layer of Türkiye's mobility super-app — strait, bay and coast.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every Turkish water surface Marti already serves on land — the Bosphorus and Princes' Islands through 16M-person Istanbul, İzmir's 4M-person bay metro, and the Bodrum and Antalya leisure coasts — with Kocaeli's İzmit Bay and Mersin as mapped next surfaces.

steady_state.vessels_at_scale: Phased build from a 4-vessel Bosphorus pilot toward a national fleet as corridors light up
steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II / N35 for the strait, bay and coastal capillaries + Quanta-LR for the longer Aegean legs
steady_state.tam_framing: Şehir Hatları carries ~40M passengers/yr, İzdeniz ~14.6M on one corridor alone, and the Aegean coast hosts one of the Mediterranean's densest leisure-boat economies — all running today on slow diesel hulls with no premium on-demand tier.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is not a pilot count — it is the whole Turkish water map. Istanbul proves the model on the world's busiest commuter waterway, İzmir doubles it in a second metro bay, and Bodrum and Antalya carry it down the leisure coast — every leg booked in the app Türkiye already rides.

markets.label: Istanbul — the Bosphorus & the Princes' Islands
markets.anchor_note: ~40M ferry passengers a year on Şehir Hatları alone — the world's busiest commuter strait, still running at diesel-vapur pace.
markets.summary: Istanbul is a 16-million-person megacity bisected by water: the Bosphorus splits Europe and Asia, and the Sea of Marmara opens onto the Princes' Islands. Cross-strait commuting is a daily fact of life — Şehir Hatları carries ~40M passengers a year across ~35 lines and fifty-plus piers — yet every crossing runs at conventional-ferry pace. The core legs are startlingly short: Eminönü–Üsküdar under a nautical mile, Karaköy–Kadıköy ~2.4nm.

hero.title: Marti × Navier — the Bosphorus, made fast.
hero.subtitle: Turn the world's busiest commuter strait into a foiling water tier and the Princes' Islands into on-demand trips — booked in the Marti app.
hero.what_we_do_together: Marti brings 4.3M riders, the wallet and scooters at every pier; Navier brings the silent zero-wake foiling fleet. Together we put a premium cross-strait tier on top of the vapur network Istanbul already lives by.

markets.why_now: Istanbul is electrifying its water — the municipality is introducing battery-electric ferries — while the premium on-demand tier remains completely unclaimed. The demand is proven at metro scale, the legs are short, and the piers already exist.

why_navier_now.the_moment: The municipal electric-vapur program proves the direction of travel; a 30+ kt foiling tier is the structural answer for time-sensitive riders the timetable can't serve.

markets.multimodal_fit: Marti scooters and mopeds already saturate both shores; the foiling pier becomes the water node in the same app — scooter to Eminönü, fly to Üsküdar, moped onward.

partner_context.their_ambition: Istanbul is Marti's home market and its densest deployment — riders, drivers and two-wheelers on both continents.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling water tier in the Marti app: cross-strait hops (Eminönü↔Üsküdar, Karaköy↔Kadıköy), the Bosphorus shore run, and on-demand Princes' Islands trips from Kabataş and Bostancı.

markets.label: İzmir & Çeşme — the bay commute and the Aegean gateway
markets.anchor_note: İZDENİZ carries ~14.6M passengers a year across İzmir bay — a proven daily water-commute culture on decades-old diesel hulls.
markets.summary: İzmir is the rare city where commuting by water is already a daily habit: the municipal İZDENİZ network carries ~14.6M passengers a year across the bay, with Konak↔Karşıyaka as the core artery. Just west, Çeşme and Alaçatı form an upscale Aegean beach scene — and Çeşme sits within a short cross-border hop of the Greek island of Chios.

hero.title: Marti × Navier — İzmir bay, upgraded.
hero.subtitle: Turn a proven 14.6M-passenger bay commute into a fast foiling tier, and Çeşme into the Aegean gateway — booked in the Marti app.
hero.what_we_do_together: Marti brings its İzmir rider base and street fleet; Navier brings the foiling fleet. Together we upgrade a water commute İzmir already loves.

markets.why_now: The demand is proven — İzmir has commuted by water since 1992 — but the experience is decades old. A premium foiling tier upgrades the proven artery and opens the Çeşme leisure line.

why_navier_now.the_moment: İzmir's bay is Türkiye's most de-risked water market: modal share already exists, so the pitch is speed and experience, not behaviour change.

markets.multimodal_fit: Marti's İzmir two-wheelers feed both Konak and Karşıyaka piers; the foiling leg slots between them in the same app.

partner_context.their_ambition: İzmir is a core Marti province — a 4M-person metro with an established water-commute culture.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling tier on the proven Konak↔Karşıyaka artery, plus the İzmir↔Çeşme/Alaçatı leisure line and the cross-border Çeşme↔Chios hop.

proof_points.claim: İzmir already commutes by water at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~14.6M İZDENİZ passengers/yr (2024); Konak↔Karşıyaka is the core artery at ~2.5nm.
The Çeşme–Chios cross-border leg is ~15nm — inside Pioneer II range — connecting the Turkish riviera to the Greek islands.

objections.concern: A municipal operator already serves the bay.
objections.response: İZDENİZ is the mass tier; we add the premium on-demand tier above it — faster, quieter, bookable to the minute.

markets.label: Bodrum & the Turquoise Coast — the charter capital

markets.summary: Bodrum and the Turquoise Coast — Datça, Göcek, Marmaris, Fethiye — are the premium yachting heartland of Türkiye, anchored by the D-Marin marina chain and flagship hospitality brands (Mandarin Oriental, Six Senses Kaplankaya, Maxx Royal, Macakizi). It is dense with high-yield guests crossing short, scenic water on slow diesel hulls.

markets.why_now: The eastern Mediterranean's charter capital still moves guests on slow diesel hops. A premium foiling tier fits the region's price points from day one.

why_navier_now.the_moment: D-Marin's marina chain and the peninsula's resort roster give ready-made pier infrastructure and captive high-yield demand.

markets.multimodal_fit: Marti mopeds and scooters already operate across Muğla province; the marina pier becomes the water node in the same app.

partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling marina mesh (Yalıkavak↔Gümüşlük↔Turgutreis↔Datça) plus resort transfers, with the longer Turquoise Coast line-haul on Quanta-LR as the roadmap.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $96M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM floor (published) — sourced corridors today
rungs.basis: sourced flagship corridors · 17% capture · today's demand

rungs.label: SOM full network (~17% capture, today, +greenfield)
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 17% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.label: SAM matured network — induced demand at scale
rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

rungs.label: Marine mobility TAM — total addressable water-transfer spend
rungs.basis: SAM divided by leading-operator capture — the full inducible water-transfer wallet at network maturity

rungs.label: Journey GMV — food, stays, and experiences (~3× TAM)
rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

rungs.label: Partner platform revenue on Navier
rungs.basis: platform commission on journey GMV routed through the Navier network (subset of full Journey GMV)

ceiling_sibling.label: Platform revenue ceiling — 18% × full Journey GMV
ceiling_sibling.derivation: journey_gmv.mid × 0.18 (full GMV ceiling, not Navier-corridor subset)
ceiling_sibling._doc: Sibling reference. Do NOT promote to a 7th ladder rung. Platform_rev rung remains the Navier-subset Interpretation-A value.

phase_economics.headline: Revenue potential by phase — conservative floor first, ecosystem prize last.
phase_economics.conversion_note: Fleet & CO2 scale from the grounded unit: 83 boats = $16M transport rev = 5,153 t CO2/yr (~$197K rev/boat).

classes.role: Capillary corridors ≤ 70nm. The workhorse of Prove + Scale.
Doubles throughput per hull on dense corridors; roughly halves payback. Scale-phase workhorse.
Regional legs 75–150nm beyond Pioneer range. Held out of near-term numbers.

vessel_sizing.range_gate_note: ≤ 70nm → Pioneer II (now). 75–150nm → Quanta-LR (roadmap). Long legs never faked on a 70nm boat.

_render_chip_flag.confidence_display: Tag every banded rung; lead with floor + corridor COUNT (ID-traceable). Never headline the 'high' band.

growth_case.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
growth_case.modal_headline: Floor to prize — every rung traces to grounded demand

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marti platform take on Navier-carried journeys
ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).
ladder_transitions._lb_ref: LB-113: partner_platform_rev_on_navier = on-Navier subset, distinct from deck's '18% × full Journey GMV' narrative ceiling
